song.title: With A Little Help From My Friends

guitar.evidence: Joe Cocker is a vocalist; his backing guitarists varied over decades without one iconic figure/instrument tied to his songs.

tone.target: warm Vox-style crunch with subtle wobble
tone.profile: warm Vox-style crunch with subtle wobble
tone.summary: A warm, mid-forward signal chain using a Tube Screamer boost into an AC30 model, enhanced by Chorus for wobble and Spring Reverb for vintage depth.
corrections: tone should be cleaner than blues-rock crunch

rig.name: Joe Cocker - With A Little Help From My Friends - Valeton GP-180

blocks.purpose: Clean up hum and background noise.
Simulate the Tube Screamer/light overdrive boost for mid-forward crunch.
blocks.gap: The GP-180 lacks a dedicated TS model, so 'Boost' is used to simulate the mid-hump and gentle drive required.

alternatives.reason: If more grit than just boost is needed.

blocks.purpose: Wah is optional and kept bypassed for flexibility.
Minimal gain stage to maintain the 'edge-of-breakup' feel without heavy fuzz.
blocks.gap: No specific low-gain dirt model is available, so a minimal setting on DST is used.

alternatives.reason: If slightly more grit than 'None' is desired.

blocks.purpose: Provides the classic Vox/British clean crunch tone.
Classic British cabinet sound to complement the AC30 model.
Adds the required subtle 'wobble' and vintage movement.
Provides the required light, vintage spring reverb.
Optional delay; kept off to avoid 'big delay' as requested.
Subtle tone shaping to enhance clarity and mid-forward presence.

improvements.summary: Upgrade the cabinet IR to better match the vintage, warm Vox/AC30 tone.

proposals.recommendedAsset: Brit 2x12 or British Vintage Cab IR
proposals.reason: The current UK 4x12 is too aggressive for the warm Vox tone.
